caveats: Share is an assumption of the scenario; survival, establishment, competition and activity of the inoculum in desert soil are not modelled.
Gate mode: any share > 0 sets gamma = 1, so the dose has no graded effect; the dose-response is the proportional mode, gamma = q/median(q) (assumes rate scales with carrier share).
Proportional mode: a non-carrier inoculum displaces the existing community and lowers uptake by about its share (a model artefact of renormalisation, not a biological prediction).
Memberships come from reasoner entailment (K and E unchanged); absence of entailment is not biological absence.
Rub' al Khali soil and community; not a prediction for other soils

plain_language: In the sample 51PRr3 the ontology finds no carbon-monoxide-oxidising organism, so the twin predicts no CO uptake at all. Adding even a tiny share of a genome known to oxidise CO opens that process (CO uptake 144 micromole per square metre over two weeks). The 'gate' result says only whether the process can run at all; the 'proportional' result says how much, assuming the rate scales with the share of such organisms. Adding an organism that is not a carrier changes nothing under the gate. Whether the added microbes would survive and establish in desert soil is not modelled: the share is an assumption of the scenario.
question: What if we add microbes that oxidise CO or H2?
